tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

# Flashback replay + editor-state formats (v0.39.10, MC 1.21.11, protocol 774)

Reverse-engineered from the CFR decompile in `tools/flashback_src/` and checked on three real replays
(`2026-10-10T14_25_31`, `T14_34_40`, `T15_04_22`). Reader: `mcstudio/flashback_replay.py`.
Editor-state writer: `mcstudio/flashback_keyframes.py`. "Verified" = checked against real files, "inferred" = from code only.

## 1. Replay zip
`<name>.zip` = `metadata.json`, `c0.flashback` (`c1`... every 6000 ticks / dimension change / config phase),
`level_chunk_caches/N`, `icon.png`.

`metadata.json` (FlashbackMeta.toJson): `uuid`, `name`, `version_string`, `world_name`, `data_version`, `protocol_version`,
`total_ticks`, `markers` (`{"<tick>": {colour, position:{position:[x,y,z], dimension}, description}}`, only when present),
`modVersions`, `customNamespacesForRegistries`, `chunks` (`{"c0.flashback": {duration, forcePlaySnapshot}}`).
The `uuid` is the file name of the editor state (section 2). Verified: uuid of T14_34_40 == `editor_states/fc524b70-....json`.

### chunk file (uncompressed, big-endian; verified)
```
int32  magic 0xD780E884 (-679417724)
varint n ; n * (varint len + utf8)      action names, index = action id
          flashback:action/{next_tick, game_packet, configuration_packet, create_local_player,
                            move_entities, level_chunk_cached, accurate_player_position_optional}
int32  snapshotSize ; snapshot bytes    state needed to start playing at the chunk (entities, tab list, ...)
actions...                               each: varint actionId, int32 size, payload[size]
```
Tick counter = number of `next_tick` actions in the action section (the snapshot does not advance time).
Verified: counts equal `total_ticks` exactly (3502 / 3544 / 2572). Actions named `*_optional` may be skipped by length.

### payloads
* `move_entities`: `varint levels; per level: identifier (dimension), varint count; per entry: varint entityId,
  f64 x,y,z, f32 yaw, f32 pitch, f32 headYaw, bool onGround`. Only entities whose pose changed are listed. It includes
  the **recording player** (feet position; yaw/pitch = look direction). Entity ids, not UUIDs. Verified: smooth tracks.
* `create_local_player`: `uuid, f64 x,y,z, f32 xRot,yRot,yHeadRot, 3*f64 velocity, GameProfile(uuid, name, props), varint gameMode`.
  Its entity id is the int in the preceding `Login` game packet (id 48). Verified (ids 4685/5681/7181, name papiguapo).
* `accurate_player_position_optional`: `varint entityId, varint n, n*(f64 x,y,z, f32 yaw,pitch)`; only when
  `recording.localPlayerUpdatesPerSecond > 20` (this install: 20, so absent).
* `game_packet`: `varint packetId + body` of a clientbound play packet. Ids for protocol 774 (from `class_9095.field_48173`):
  1 add_entity, 2 animate, 25 damage_event, 34 entity_event, 36 explode, 41 hurt_animation, 48 login, 68 player_info_update,
  75 remove_entities, 80 respawn, 97 set_entity_data, 119 system_chat, 122 take_item_entity.
  Entity type id = registration order of `class_1299` (player = 155).
* **Packets Flashback never records** (`IgnoredPacketSet.IGNORED`): sounds, player_chat, set_health, set_experience,
  combat_kill, player_position, level_event, container packets. Consequences (verified): health comes from `set_entity_data`
  index 9 (float) of the local entity; deaths appear as `system_chat` `death.attack.*(name)` plus health 0; no chat/sound events.

### events the reader derives (verified on real data)
damage (health drop, cause entity type from damage_event, e.g. skeleton/creeper), death, respawn, teleport (>12 block jump in one tick),
explosion, kill, pickup, mob_near, lightning, player join/leave, markers. Session 14_34_40: 6 hurt animations, skeleton and creeper damage,
one explosion 5.7 blocks away, 2 salmon kills.

## 2. Editor state file
`<.minecraft>/flashback/editor_states/<replay uuid>.json` (+ `.json.old`). `EditorStateManager.get(uuid)` runs inside
`Flashback.openReplayWorld`; the file is compact Gson JSON of `EditorState`. Autosave: every 30 s when dirty, and on `reset()`.

```
{ replayVisuals:{...ReplayVisuals fields...}, sceneLock:{}, scenes:[Scene...], sceneIndex, zoomMin, zoomMax,
  usedByPaths:[abs zip paths], hideDuringExport:[uuid], hideAllSpectators, muteVoice, hideNametags, skinOverride, ... }
Scene = { name, keyframeTracks:[Track], exportStartTicks, exportEndTicks (-1 = unset), history:{entries:[],position} }
Track = { keyframeType: CAMERA|CAMERA_ORBIT|TRACK_ENTITY|CAMERA_SHAKE|FOV|SPEED|TIMELAPSE|TIME_OF_DAY|FREEZE|BLOCK_OVERRIDE|AUDIO,
          keyframesByTick:{"<tick>": Keyframe}, enabled, customColour [, customName] }
```
* Time unit = **replay ticks** (20/s). One scene = one shot (own tracks, own export range). Verified: the file the creator's session
  produced has this exact shape; `flashback_keyframes.validate_state` accepts it, top-level and `replayVisuals` key order match,
  and re-serialising it is byte-identical.
* `EditorScene`/`KeyframeTrack` have no no-arg constructor, so Gson allocates them via Unsafe and skips initialisers:
  omitting `enabled`/`history`/`keyframesByTick` gives a silently disabled track or an NPE (inferred from code).
* Keyframes carry `type` and an optional `interpolation_type` (SMOOTH, LINEAR, EASE_IN, EASE_OUT, EASE_IN_OUT, HOLD, HERMITE):
  `camera {position[3] (feet), yaw, pitch, roll}`; `camera_orbit {center[3], distance, yaw, pitch}`;
  `track_entity {target uuid, bodyPart HEAD|BODY|ROOT, yawOffset, pitchOffset, positionOffset[3], viewOffset[3], roll}`;
  `fov {fov 1..110}`; `tickrate {tickrate}` (SPEED track; replay ticks per real second, 20 = 1x);
  `freeze {freeze, freezeDelay}`; `timelapse {ticks}` (keyframe at timeline tick K means video time = ticks/20; speed = dK/dT*20);
  `time {time}`; `camera_shake {frequencyX, amplitudeX, frequencyY, amplitudeY[, splitParams]}`.
* Camera math (from `KeyframeChangeCameraPosition*` and `KeyframeChangeTrackEntity`): camera eye = feet + 1.62; orbit eye =
  center - look(yaw,pitch)*distance with look = (-sin yaw*cos p, -sin p, cos yaw*cos p); track_entity viewOffset z>0 = behind the
  entity, rotated by pitch. SMOOTH = centripetal Catmull-Rom (`spline/CatmullRom`), ported as `evaluate_track`.
* Export range = `exportStartTicks/exportEndTicks` of the current scene if set, else first/last keyframe of enabled tracks, else the
  whole replay. At most one change per class is applied per frame; later camera-type tracks override earlier ones.
* Timeline clipboard (Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V): `{"relativePosition":null,"relativeYaw":null,"relativePitch":null,
  "savedTracks":[{"type":"CAMERA","track":0,"copiedFromDisabled":false,"keyframes":{"0":{...keyframe...}}}]}`, pasted at the cursor tick.
* `config/flashback/flashback.json`: `internalExport` stores the last export dialog values (resolution, framerate, container,
  videoCodec, selectedVideoEncoder, useMaximumBitrate, noGui, ssaa, recordAudio, defaultExportPath); the bitrate text field is not
  persisted (default `20m`). `forceDefaultExportSettings` re-applies chosen fields every time the dialog opens.
  Recording: `recordingControls.automaticallyStart` is currently false here and `quicksave` false (a "Save replay" screen
  appears after each session).

## 3. Replay Mod `.mcpr` comparison (session 15_02_10)
`.mcpr` = zip: `metaData.json` (serverName, duration ms, date epoch ms, mcversion, protocol 774, generator), `recording.tmcpr`
(repeated `int32 timestampMs, int32 length, packet[length]`, packet = varint id + raw clientbound packet), `markers.json`, `mods.json`.
Same protocol ids as above (verified: 76735 packets; ids 81/52/99/51/35 dominate = rotate_head/move_pos_rot/motion/move_pos/position_sync).

| | Flashback | Replay Mod |
|---|---|---|
| clock | 20 Hz ticks (`next_tick`), exact | real-time ms stamps, no tick boundaries |
| entity pose | absolute doubles per tick in one action | relative short deltas (1/4096) plus teleports; must be integrated, entity ids tracked |
| local player | explicit `create_local_player` + positions | not an entity in the stream (selfId -1); needs extra work (not done) |
| ignored packets | sounds/health/chat dropped | everything kept (chat, sounds, set_health) |
| size | 1.4-5 MB per ~3000 ticks (+35 MB chunk cache) | 44 MB |
| reader effort | done | roughly 2-3x more; only worth it for chat/sound events |

Recommendation: use Flashback replays for positions and automation; keep the .mcpr only as a fallback.

def queue_jobs(slug: str, plan: dict | None = None, replay=None, retry_rejected: bool = False) -> list[Path]:
    """Write studio/cinematic_jobs/<slug>/job-XX.json for every shot still to render; marks them `queued`."""
    plan = plan or load_shots(slug)
    if not plan:
        raise SystemExit(f"{slug}: no shots.json - run: mcs cinematic plan {slug}")
    if replay is None and plan.get("replay") and plan.get("replay_kind") == "flashback" and Path(plan["replay"]).exists():
        try:
            replay = load_replay(plan["replay"])
        except Exception:                                            # noqa: BLE001
            replay = None
    jd = job_dir(slug)
    jd.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out = []
    redo = {"planned", "queued", "failed"} | ({"rejected"} if retry_rejected else set())
    for i, s in enumerate(plan["shots"], 1):
        if s["status"] not in redo:
            continue
        vis = s["params"]["visuals"]
        job = {"version": 1, "job_id": f"job-{i:02d}", "project": slug, "shot_id": s["id"], "kind": s["kind"],
               "replay": {"path": plan.get("replay"), "kind": plan.get("replay_kind")},
               "tick_start": s["replay_tick"], "ticks": s["ticks"],
               "tick_end": None if s["replay_tick"] is None else s["replay_tick"] + (
                   s["params"].get("replay_ticks_covered") or s["ticks"]),
               "dur_s": s["dur_s"], "anchor": s["params"].get("anchor"),
               "camera": {"abstract": s["params"]["camera"], "keyframes": _try_keyframes(s, replay)},
               "visuals": {"hide_gui": vis["hide_gui"], "hide_nametags": vis["hide_nametags"],
                           "hide_chat": vis["hide_chat"], "night_vision": vis["night_vision"],
                           "time_of_day_override": vis["time_of_day"]},
               "export": {"width": 1920, "height": 1080, "fps": s["params"]["fps"], "codec": "h264",
                          "output": f"broll/{s['id']}.mp4",
                          "output_abs": str((PROJECTS / slug / "broll" / f"{s['id']}.mp4").resolve())},
               "status": "queued"}
        p = jd / f"{job['job_id']}.json"
        _write(p, job)
        s["status"], s["job"] = "queued", p.name
        out.append(p)
    _write(shots_path(slug), plan)
    return out

def _ff(args: list, timeout: int = 600) -> None:
    r = subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-y", *map(str, args)], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
    if r.returncode:
        raise RuntimeError(f"ffmpeg failed: {r.stderr.strip()[-600:]}")


class FakeExporter(Exporter):
    """Placeholder clip: moving colour gradient + big text (kind, shot id, tick). Correct size / fps / duration, so the rest
    of the pipeline (QA, splice, render) can be exercised without Minecraft. job['fake_defect'] in
    {black, static, uniform} produces the matching bad clip for QA tests."""
    name = "fake"
    FONT = "C\\:/Windows/Fonts/arial.ttf"

    def render(self, job: dict) -> Path:
        ex = job["export"]
        out = Path(ex["output_abs"])
        out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        w, h, fps, d = ex["width"], ex["height"], ex["fps"], job["dur_s"]
        c0, c1 = _KIND_COLORS.get(job["kind"], ("0x444444", "0xdddddd"))
        defect = job.get("fake_defect")
        lines = [job["kind"].upper().replace("_", " "), f"{job['shot_id']}   tick {job.get('tick_start')}",
                 f"{job['project']}  {d:.1f}s @ {fps}fps  [PLACEHOLDER]"]

        def txt(s, y, size):
            s = s.replace(":", "\\:")
            return (f"drawtext=fontfile='{self.FONT}':text='{s}':fontcolor=white:fontsize={size}:"
                    f"x=(w-text_w)/2:y={y}:borderw=4:bordercolor=black")
        label = ",".join([txt(lines[0], "h*0.30", 110), txt(lines[1], "h*0.46", 64), txt(lines[2], "h*0.58", 40)])
        mover = f"drawbox=x='mod(t*320,{w})':y=h*0.80:w=160:h=40:color=white@0.9:t=fill"
        if defect == "black":
            src = f"color=c=black:s={w}x{h}:r={fps}:d={d}"
            vf = "noise=alls=2:allf=t"
        elif defect == "static":
            src = f"color=c=0x3a7bd5:s={w}x{h}:r={fps}:d={d}"
            vf = txt(lines[0], "h*0.4", 100)
        elif defect == "uniform":
            src = f"color=c=0x6b4f2a:s={w}x{h}:r={fps}:d={d}"
            vf = f"noise=alls=3:allf=t,{mover}"
        else:
            src = f"gradients=s={w}x{h}:r={fps}:d={d}:c0={c0}:c1={c1}:speed=0.35:type=linear"
            vf = f"{mover},{label}"
        _ff(["-f", "lavfi", "-i", src, "-vf", vf + ",format=yuv420p", "-an", "-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "veryfast",
             "-crf", "20", "-threads", "2", "-movflags", "+faststart", "-t", d, out])
        return out


class ManualExporter(Exporter):
    """Writes a plain-language checklist a human follows inside Flashback; the exported file is picked up on the next
    `mcs cinematic render` because it lands at the job's output path."""
    name = "manual"

    def render(self, job: dict) -> Path | None:
        out = Path(job["export"]["output_abs"])
        if out.exists():
            return out
        md = job_dir(job["project"]) / "CHECKLIST.md"
        lines = md.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if md.exists() else [
            f"# Manual Flashback exports for {job['project']}", "",
            "In Flashback: open the replay, press Edit, then for each item below set the range, add the camera",
            "keyframes described, tick Hide GUI / nametags / chat, export 1920x1080 H.264 to the given file.", ""]
        head = f"## {job['job_id']} - {job['kind'].replace('_', ' ')} ({job['dur_s']:.1f}s)"
        if head not in lines:
            cam = job["camera"]["abstract"]
            vis = job["visuals"]
            lines += [head,
                      f"- Replay: `{job['replay'].get('path')}`",
                      f"- Range: tick {job['tick_start']} to {job['tick_end']}  ({job['ticks']} ticks = {job['dur_s']:.1f}s)",
                      f"- Camera: {cam.get('move')} around the player; details `{json.dumps(cam)}`",
                      f"- Anchor (player at that tick): {job.get('anchor')}",
                      "- Visuals: GUI off, nametags off, chat off" + (", night vision ON" if vis["night_vision"] else "")
                      + (f", time of day {vis['time_of_day_override']}" if vis["time_of_day_override"] else ""),
                      f"- Export: {job['export']['width']}x{job['export']['height']} @ {job['export']['fps']} fps H.264",
                      f"- Save as: `{job['export']['output_abs']}`", ""]
        md.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        return None

def render_queue(slug: str, exporter: str | None = None, force: bool = False) -> dict:
    """Run the chosen exporter over queued jobs, QA each clip, update shots.json. Returns counts."""
    plan = load_shots(slug)
    if not plan:
        raise SystemExit(f"{slug}: no shots.json - run: mcs cinematic plan {slug}")
    C = cfg(SET.load(slug))
    name = exporter or C["exporter"]
    if name not in EXPORTERS:
        raise SystemExit(f"unknown exporter {name!r}; choose from {sorted(EXPORTERS)}")
    if C["render_only_when_idle"] and name != "manual" and not force and not machine_idle():
        print("[cinematic] Minecraft or OBS is running - not rendering now (settings: render_only_when_idle). "
              "Use --force to override.")
        return {"rendered": 0, "rejected": 0, "failed": 0, "waiting": 0, "deferred": True}
    exp = EXPORTERS[name]()
    ref = project_ref_luma(slug)
    counts = {"rendered": 0, "rejected": 0, "failed": 0, "waiting": 0}
    for s in plan["shots"]:
        if s["status"] not in ("queued", "failed"):
            continue

            continue
        ex = job["export"]

        s.pop("note", None)

            s["note"] = "; ".join(qa["reasons"])
        counts[s["status"]] += 1

@dataclass
class ExportOptions:
    """Per-job export settings consumed by the flashback_auto mod (maps 1:1 onto ExportSettings)."""

    width: int = 1920
    height: int = 1080
    fps: float = 60.0
    container: str = "MP4"
    codec: str = "H264"
    encoder: str | None = None        # e.g. "libx264", "h264_amf" (None -> Flashback's first valid encoder)
    bitrate: int = 20_000_000
    ssaa: bool = False
    no_gui: bool = True
    reset_rng: bool = False
    record_audio: bool = False
    transparent: bool = False


def jobs_json(replay_path: str | Path, shots: Sequence[Shot], out_dir: str | Path,
              opts: ExportOptions | None = None, prefix: str = "") -> dict:
    """Job list for the flashback_auto mod: one job per scene/shot, rendered to <out_dir>/<prefix><shot>.mp4."""
    opts = opts or ExportOptions()
    out_dir = Path(out_dir)
    jobs = []
    for i, s in enumerate(shots):
        safe = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_.@-]+", "_", f"{prefix}{i:02d}_{s.name}")
        jobs.append({
            "scene": i, "name": safe, "start": s.start, "end": s.end,
            "output": str(out_dir / f"{safe}.{opts.container.lower() if opts.container != 'PNG_SEQUENCE' else 'png'}"),
            "width": opts.width, "height": opts.height, "fps": opts.fps, "container": opts.container,
            "codec": opts.codec, "encoder": opts.encoder, "bitrate": opts.bitrate, "ssaa": opts.ssaa,
            "noGui": opts.no_gui, "resetRng": opts.reset_rng, "recordAudio": opts.record_audio,
            "transparent": opts.transparent, "kind": s.kind, "note": s.note,
        })
    return {"version": 1, "replay": str(replay_path), "jobs": jobs}

"""Build flashback_auto without Gradle/Loom, using only the Java 21 runtime bundled with Minecraft (javac/jar/javap).

    cd studio
    .venv/Scripts/python.exe tools/flashback_auto/build.py            # compile + self test + jar
    .venv/Scripts/python.exe tools/flashback_auto/build.py --no-test

Output: tools/flashback_auto/build/flashback_auto-<version>.jar   (nothing is copied anywhere else, nothing is downloaded).
Compiles against jars already on disk (Minecraft intermediary client jar, Flashback, Fabric loader, gson, log4j-api, ...).
Fabric runs on intermediary names, so the source uses class_310 etc. directly (see AutoRunner javadoc for the list).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent

INTERMEDIARY = MC / ".fabric/remappedJars/minecraft-1.21.11-0.19.2/client-intermediary.jar"

    ("com/google/code/gson/gson/2.13.2/gson-2.13.2.jar", True),

def tool(name: str) -> str:
    p = JAVA_BIN / f"{name}.exe"

    return str(p)

def dumps_state(state: dict) -> str:
    """Compact JSON like ``FlashbackGson.COMPRESSED`` (no spaces, doubles keep '.0')."""
    return json.dumps(state, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)


def write_state(state: dict, replay_uuid: str, folder: str | Path) -> Path:
    """Write ``<folder>/<replay_uuid>.json``. ``folder`` must be ``<.minecraft>/flashback/editor_states``
    for Flashback to pick it up -- this function does not default to it on purpose.
    The previous file (if any) is kept as ``.json.old`` exactly like EditorStateManager.save() does."""
    errs = validate_state(state)
    if errs:
        raise ValueError("invalid editor state:\n  " + "\n  ".join(errs))
    folder = Path(folder)
    folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    p = folder / f"{replay_uuid}.json"
    if p.exists():
        p.replace(folder / f"{replay_uuid}.json.old")
    p.write_text(dumps_state(state), encoding="utf-8")
    return p

"""Start Minecraft 1.21.11 (the creator's Fabric profile) in flashback_auto render mode WITHOUT TLauncher's GUI.

    cd studio
    .venv/Scripts/python.exe tools/flashback_auto/launch_render.py --job cinematic_jobs/<slug>/jobs.json            # dry run (default)
    .venv/Scripts/python.exe tools/flashback_auto/launch_render.py --job ... --launch                                # real launch

Dry run (the default) builds the exact command line, checks every referenced file and prints the result. Nothing is started,
nothing is written. A real launch needs --launch AND a fresh ``ARMED`` marker next to the job file (``mcstudio.flashback_export``
writes it right before it calls ``launch``; ``--arm`` does the same from the command line).

How the command is built (all read from disk, nothing hard-coded except the defaults below):
* ``.minecraft/versions/Fabric 1.21.11/Fabric 1.21.11.json`` -- main class (KnotClient), JVM args, game args, 115 libraries.
  The JSON is TLauncher's flattened format: argument entries are ``{"values": [...], "rules": [...]}`` and every library is just
  ``name`` (+``url``); the jar path is derived from the Maven coordinates under ``.minecraft/libraries``. It does not inherit
  from a parent JSON (``inheritsFrom`` is supported if it ever appears). ``TLauncherAdditional.json`` says ``"jar": "1.21.11"``,
  i.e. the vanilla client jar ``versions/1.21.11/1.21.11.jar`` goes on the classpath.
* Java: the runtime Mojang/TLauncher downloaded (``.minecraft/runtime/java-runtime-delta``, Java 21).
* Natives: ``versions/Fabric 1.21.11/natives`` (already extracted by TLauncher; LWJGL 3.3 also self-extracts from its jars).
* Auth: none. Offline ``--uuid`` (Java ``UUID.nameUUIDFromBytes("OfflinePlayer:<name>")``), ``--accessToken 0``, ``--userType legacy``.
  The replay viewer never talks to Mojang, so no TLauncher-specific library or token is needed (TLauncher's skin/auth patcher is not
  in this profile's library list). The only TLauncher dependency is that it already downloaded everything.
* The mod jar is injected with ``-Dfabric.addMods=<jar>`` (Fabric loader's ArgumentModCandidateFinder), so nothing has to be copied
  into ``.minecraft/mods``. If a copy of the jar IS in mods/, the property is left out (Fabric rejects duplicate mod ids).
* Memory ``-Xmx6G`` (TLauncher's ~21 GB is far more than a replay export needs), below-normal CPU priority, no console window.

Real launch refuses to start when another Minecraft is running (javaw/java whose command line mentions minecraft).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import uuid
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
STUDIO = HERE.parents[1]

MC_DIR = Path(os.environ.get("APPDATA", str(Path.home() / "AppData/Roaming"))) / ".minecraft"
VERSION_NAME = "Fabric 1.21.11"
DEFAULT_USERNAME = "papiguapo"        # the name the replays were recorded under (any name works offline)
DEFAULT_XMX = "6G"
DEFAULT_XMS = "1G"
MOD_ID = "flashback_auto"
MOD_VERSION = "0.1.0"
DEFAULT_MOD_JAR = HERE / "build" / f"{MOD_ID}-{MOD_VERSION}.jar"
ARMED = "ARMED"

CREATE_NO_WINDOW = 0x08000000
BELOW_NORMAL_PRIORITY_CLASS = 0x00004000
CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP = 0x00000200


class LaunchError(RuntimeError):
    pass


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ version json
def _read_json(p: Path) -> dict:
    return json.loads(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


def load_version(mc_dir: Path = MC_DIR, name: str = VERSION_NAME) -> dict:
    """Version JSON with ``inheritsFrom`` merged (libraries/arguments of the parent first)."""
    p = mc_dir / "versions" / name / f"{name}.json"
    if not p.is_file():
        raise LaunchError(f"version json not found: {p}")
    v = _read_json(p)
    if v.get("inheritsFrom"):
        parent = load_version(mc_dir, v["inheritsFrom"])
        merged = dict(parent)
        merged.update({k: x for k, x in v.items() if k not in ("libraries", "arguments")})
        merged["libraries"] = list(parent.get("libraries", [])) + list(v.get("libraries", []))
        pa, va = parent.get("arguments", {}), v.get("arguments", {})
        merged["arguments"] = {k: list(pa.get(k, [])) + list(va.get(k, [])) for k in ("game", "jvm")}
        v = merged
    return v


def _rules_allow(rules, features: dict | None = None) -> bool:
    """Mojang rule semantics for Windows x64, no optional features enabled."""
    if not rules:
        return True
    features = features or {}
    allowed = False
    for r in rules:
        ok = True
        os_r = r.get("os")
        if os_r:
            if os_r.get("name") not in (None, "windows"):
                ok = False
            if os_r.get("arch") not in (None, "x86_64", "amd64"):
                ok = False
        feat = r.get("features")
        if feat and any(features.get(k, False) != want for k, want in feat.items()):
            ok = False
        if ok:
            allowed = r.get("action", "allow") == "allow"
    return allowed


def library_path(lib: dict, libs_dir: Path) -> Path | None:
    """Jar path for a library entry, or None when this platform should not load it."""
    if not _rules_allow(lib.get("rules")):
        return None
    art = lib.get("artifact") or (lib.get("downloads") or {}).get("artifact")
    if art and art.get("path"):
        return libs_dir / art["path"]
    parts = lib["name"].split(":")
    if len(parts) < 3:
        raise LaunchError(f"unparsable library name {lib['name']!r}")
    group, artifact, version = parts[:3]
    classifier = parts[3] if len(parts) > 3 else None
    if classifier:
        # natives-windows only (x64); linux/macos/arm64/x86 variants are not for this machine
        if classifier.startswith("natives-"):
            if classifier != "natives-windows":
                return None
        elif not classifier.startswith("windows"):
            return None
    fn = f"{artifact}-{version}" + (f"-{classifier}" if classifier else "") + ".jar"
    return libs_dir / Path(*group.split(".")) / artifact / version / fn


def _args(entries, features: dict | None = None) -> list[str]:
    out: list[str] = []
    for e in entries:
        if isinstance(e, str):
            out.append(e)
            continue
        if not _rules_allow(e.get("rules"), features):
            continue
        val = e.get("values", e.get("value"))
        out.extend([val] if isinstance(val, str) else list(val or []))
    return out


def offline_uuid(name: str) -> str:
    """java.util.UUID.nameUUIDFromBytes(("OfflinePlayer:" + name).getBytes(UTF_8)), as the vanilla/offline convention."""
    d = bytearray(hashlib.md5(("OfflinePlayer:" + name).encode("utf-8")).digest())
    d[6] = (d[6] & 0x0F) | 0x30
    d[8] = (d[8] & 0x3F) | 0x80
    return str(uuid.UUID(bytes=bytes(d)))


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ plan
@dataclass
class LaunchPlan:
    java: Path
    args: list[str]                       # everything after java (JVM args, -cp, main class, game args)
    cwd: Path
    classpath: list[Path] = field(default_factory=list)
    natives_dir: Path | None = None
    job_file: Path | None = None
    mod_jar: Path | None = None
    mod_mode: str = "addMods"             # addMods | installed
    missing: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    notes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)

    @property
    def command(self) -> list[str]:
        return [str(self.java), *self.args]

    def as_text(self) -> str:
        return subprocess.list2cmdline(self.command)


def build_plan(job_file: str | Path, token: str | None = None, *, mc_dir: Path = MC_DIR, version: str = VERSION_NAME,
               username: str = DEFAULT_USERNAME, game_uuid: str | None = None, xmx: str = DEFAULT_XMX, xms: str = DEFAULT_XMS,
               mod_jar: str | Path | None = None, extra_jvm: list[str] | None = None, width: int | None = None,
               height: int | None = None) -> LaunchPlan:
    job_file = Path(job_file).resolve()
    vdir = mc_dir / "versions" / version
    v = load_version(mc_dir, version)
    missing: list[str] = []
    notes: list[str] = []

    def need(p: Path, what: str) -> Path:
        if not p.exists():
            missing.append(f"{what}: {p}")
        return p

    java = need(mc_dir / "runtime" / "java-runtime-delta" / "windows" / "java-runtime-delta" / "bin" / "java.exe", "java")
    need(job_file, "job file")

    # classpath: libraries (v.libraries order) + client jar
    libs_dir = mc_dir / "libraries"
    cp: list[Path] = []
    seen: set[str] = set()
    for lib in v["libraries"]:
        p = library_path(lib, libs_dir)
        if p is None or str(p).lower() in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(str(p).lower())
        need(p, "library")
        cp.append(p)
    add = vdir / "TLauncherAdditional.json"
    jar_name = (_read_json(add).get("jar") if add.is_file() else None) or v.get("jar") or version
    client_jar = need(mc_dir / "versions" / jar_name / f"{jar_name}.jar", "client jar")
    cp.append(client_jar)

    # natives
    natives = vdir / "natives"
    if not natives.is_dir() or not any(natives.glob("lwjgl*.dll")):
        natives = HERE / "natives"
        notes.append(f"TLauncher natives dir missing, LWJGL will self-extract into {natives}")
        natives.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) if False else None  # dry run never creates folders; launch() does

    assets = mc_dir / "assets"
    index_id = v.get("assetIndex", {}).get("id") or v.get("assets")
    need(assets / "indexes" / f"{index_id}.json", "asset index")
    log_cfg = None
    lg = (v.get("logging") or {}).get("client")
    if lg and lg.get("file", {}).get("id"):
        log_cfg = assets / "log_configs" / lg["file"]["id"]
        if not log_cfg.exists():
            notes.append(f"log4j config {log_cfg.name} missing, using default logging")
            log_cfg = None

    # mod jar injection
    jar = Path(mod_jar).resolve() if mod_jar else DEFAULT_MOD_JAR
    installed = [p for p in (mc_dir / "mods").glob("flashback_auto*.jar")] if (mc_dir / "mods").is_dir() else []
    mod_mode = "installed" if installed else "addMods"
    if mod_mode == "addMods":
        need(jar, "mod jar (build it: python tools/flashback_auto/build.py)")
    else:
        notes.append(f"mod jar already installed in mods/: {installed[0].name}; -Dfabric.addMods not used")

    subst = {
        "auth_player_name": username,
        "version_name": version,
        "game_directory": str(mc_dir),
        "assets_root": str(assets),
        "assets_index_name": str(index_id),
        "auth_uuid": game_uuid or offline_uuid(username),
        "auth_access_token": "0",
        "clientid": "0",
        "auth_xuid": "0",
        "version_type": str(v.get("type", "release")),
        "natives_directory": str(natives),
        "launcher_name": "flashback_auto",
        "launcher_version": MOD_VERSION,
        "classpath": os.pathsep.join(str(p) for p in cp),
        "user_type": "legacy",
        "resolution_width": str(width or ""),
        "resolution_height": str(height or ""),
    }

    def sub(s: str) -> str:
        return re.sub(r"\$\{(\w+)\}", lambda m: subst.get(m.group(1), m.group(0)), s)

    features = {"has_custom_resolution": bool(width and height)}
    jvm = [sub(a) for a in _args(v.get("arguments", {}).get("jvm", []), features)]
    game = [sub(a) for a in _args(v.get("arguments", {}).get("game", []), features)]
    left = [a for a in jvm + game if re.search(r"\$\{\w+\}", a)]
    if left:
        missing.append(f"unresolved placeholders: {left}")
    if "--userType" not in game:
        game += ["--userType", "legacy"]

    ours = [f"-Xmx{xmx}", f"-Xms{xms}", "-XX:+UseG1GC", "-Dfile.encoding=UTF-8",
            f"-D{'flashback_auto.job'}={job_file}"]
    if token:
        ours.append(f"-Dflashback_auto.token={token}")
    if mod_mode == "addMods":
        ours.append(f"-Dfabric.addMods={jar}")
    if log_cfg:
        ours.append(f"-Dlog4j.configurationFile={log_cfg}")
    ours += list(extra_jvm or [])

    # JVM args from the profile go first, ours after (later -X flags win), then -cp is already inside `jvm`
    args = ours + jvm + [v["mainClass"]] + game
    return LaunchPlan(java=java, args=args, cwd=mc_dir, classpath=cp, natives_dir=natives, job_file=job_file,
                      mod_jar=jar if mod_mode == "addMods" else installed[0], mod_mode=mod_mode, missing=missing, notes=notes)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ safety checks
def _powershell_processes() -> list[dict]:
    script = ("@(Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter \"Name='javaw.exe' OR Name='java.exe'\" | ForEach-Object "
              "{ [pscustomobject]@{pid=[int]$_.ProcessId;name=$_.Name;cmd=[string]$_.CommandLine} }) | ConvertTo-Json -Compress")
    try:
        r = subprocess.run(["powershell", "-NoProfile", "-NonInteractive", "-Command", script], capture_output=True, text=True,
                           timeout=30, creationflags=CREATE_NO_WINDOW, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired) as e:
        raise LaunchError(f"cannot list running processes ({e}); refusing to launch blind") from e
    out = (r.stdout or "").strip()
    if not out:
        return []
    try:
        d = json.loads(out)
    except ValueError as e:
        raise LaunchError(f"cannot parse the process list ({out[:100]!r}); refusing to launch blind") from e
    return [d] if isinstance(d, dict) else list(d)


def running_minecraft(list_processes=None) -> list[dict]:
    """java/javaw processes whose command line mentions minecraft (the TLauncher game or ours)."""
    procs = (list_processes or _powershell_processes)()
    hits = []
    for p in procs:
        cmd = (p.get("cmd") or "").lower()
        if "minecraft" in cmd:
            hits.append({"pid": p.get("pid"), "name": p.get("name"), "cmd": (p.get("cmd") or "")[:200]})
    return hits


def check_plan(plan: LaunchPlan) -> list[str]:
    """Problems that would stop a launch (missing files)."""
    return list(plan.missing)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ arming
def write_armed(job_file: str | Path, token: str | None = None, now: float | None = None) -> Path:
    """Write ``ARMED`` next to the job file. The mod needs this AND -Dflashback_auto.job (and matching token) to do anything."""
    job_file = Path(job_file).resolve()
    p = job_file.with_name(ARMED)
    body = {"job": str(job_file), "created": int(now if now is not None else time.time()), "pid": os.getpid()}
    if token:
        body["token"] = token
    p.write_text(json.dumps(body), encoding="utf-8")
    return p


def disarm(job_file: str | Path) -> None:
    try:
        Path(job_file).resolve().with_name(ARMED).unlink()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        pass


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ launching
class GameProcess:
    """Thin wrapper over the Popen handle (also what tests replace with a fake)."""

    def __init__(self, popen: subprocess.Popen):
        self._p = popen
        self.pid = popen.pid

    def poll(self):
        return self._p.poll()

    def wait(self, timeout=None):
        return self._p.wait(timeout)

    def kill_tree(self) -> None:
        if self._p.poll() is None:
            subprocess.run(["taskkill", "/PID", str(self.pid), "/T", "/F"], capture_output=True, creationflags=CREATE_NO_WINDOW)
            try:
                self._p.wait(15)
            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                self._p.kill()


def launch(plan: LaunchPlan, log_path: str | Path | None = None, *, list_processes=None, popen=subprocess.Popen) -> GameProcess:
    """Start the game. Refuses on missing files or when another Minecraft is running."""
    probs = check_plan(plan)
    if probs:
        raise LaunchError("cannot launch, missing:\n  " + "\n  ".join(probs))
    other = running_minecraft(list_processes)
    if other:
        raise LaunchError("another Minecraft is already running, not launching: "
                          + "; ".join(f"pid {o['pid']} {o['name']}" for o in other))
    if plan.natives_dir and not plan.natives_dir.exists():
        plan.natives_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out = open(log_path, "ab") if log_path else subprocess.DEVNULL
    try:
        p = popen(plan.command, cwd=str(plan.cwd), stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=out, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
                  creationflags=CREATE_NO_WINDOW | BELOW_NORMAL_PRIORITY_CLASS | CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP)
    finally:
        if log_path:
            out.close()
    return GameProcess(p)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ cli
def _redact(cmd: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    out = []
    skip = False
    for a in cmd:
        if skip:
            out.append("***")
            skip = False
            continue
        out.append(a)
        if a == "--accessToken":
            skip = True
    return out


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("--job", required=True, help="job file written by flashback_keyframes.jobs_json")
    ap.add_argument("--launch", action="store_true", help="really start Minecraft (default: dry run)")
    ap.add_argument("--arm", action="store_true", help="with --launch: write the ARMED marker first (the exporter normally does this)")
    ap.add_argument("--xmx", default=DEFAULT_XMX)
    ap.add_argument("--username", default=DEFAULT_USERNAME)
    ap.add_argument("--mod-jar", default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="print the plan as JSON")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)

    token = uuid.uuid4().hex if a.launch else "DRYRUN"
    plan = build_plan(a.job, token, username=a.username, xmx=a.xmx, mod_jar=a.mod_jar)
    if a.json:
        print(json.dumps({"java": str(plan.java), "args": _redact(plan.args), "cwd": str(plan.cwd), "missing": plan.missing,
                          "notes": plan.notes, "mod_mode": plan.mod_mode}, indent=2))
    else:
        print("mode:", "LAUNCH" if a.launch else "dry run (nothing started)")
        print("java:", plan.java)
        print("cwd :", plan.cwd)
        print("mod :", plan.mod_jar, f"({plan.mod_mode})")
        print("classpath entries:", len(plan.classpath), "| natives:", plan.natives_dir)
        for n in plan.notes:
            print("note:", n)
        print("command:")
        print(subprocess.list2cmdline(_redact(plan.command)))
    if plan.missing:
        print(f"\nPROBLEMS ({len(plan.missing)}):", file=sys.stderr)
        for m in plan.missing:
            print("  -", m, file=sys.stderr)
    else:
        print(f"\nOK: all {len(plan.classpath)} classpath files, java, assets index and mod jar exist.")
    if not a.launch:
        return 1 if plan.missing else 0
    if a.arm:
        write_armed(a.job, token)
    try:
        proc = launch(plan, Path(a.job).resolve().with_name("game_stdout.log"))
    except LaunchError as e:
        print("REFUSED:", e, file=sys.stderr)
        if a.arm:
            disarm(a.job)
        return 2
    print(f"started pid {proc.pid}; status: {Path(a.job).resolve().with_name('status.json')}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

    """Mojang rule semantics for Windows x64, no optional features enabled."""
    if not rules:
        return True
    features = features or {}
    allowed = False
    for r in rules:
        ok = True
        os_r = r.get("os")
        if os_r:
            if os_r.get("name") not in (None, "windows"):
                ok = False
            if os_r.get("arch") not in (None, "x86_64", "amd64"):
                ok = False
        feat = r.get("features")
        if feat and any(features.get(k, False) != want for k, want in feat.items()):
            ok = False
        if ok:
            allowed = r.get("action", "allow") == "allow"
    return allowed


def library_path(lib: dict, libs_dir: Path) -> Path | None:
    """Jar path for a library entry, or None when this platform should not load it."""
    if not _rules_allow(lib.get("rules")):
        return None
    art = lib.get("artifact") or (lib.get("downloads") or {}).get("artifact")
    if art and art.get("path"):
        return libs_dir / art["path"]
    parts = lib["name"].split(":")
    if len(parts) < 3:
        raise LaunchError(f"unparsable library name {lib['name']!r}")
    group, artifact, version = parts[:3]
    classifier = parts[3] if len(parts) > 3 else None
    if classifier:
        # natives-windows only (x64); linux/macos/arm64/x86 variants are not for this machine
        if classifier.startswith("natives-"):
            if classifier != "natives-windows":
                return None
        elif not classifier.startswith("windows"):
            return None
    fn = f"{artifact}-{version}" + (f"-{classifier}" if classifier else "") + ".jar"
    return libs_dir / Path(*group.split(".")) / artifact / version / fn


def _args(entries, features: dict | None = None) -> list[str]:
    out: list[str] = []
    for e in entries:
        if isinstance(e, str):
            out.append(e)
            continue
        if not _rules_allow(e.get("rules"), features):
            continue
        val = e.get("values", e.get("value"))
        out.extend([val] if isinstance(val, str) else list(val or []))
    return out


def offline_uuid(name: str) -> str:
    """java.util.UUID.nameUUIDFromBytes(("OfflinePlayer:" + name).getBytes(UTF_8)), as the vanilla/offline convention."""
    d = bytearray(hashlib.md5(("OfflinePlayer:" + name).encode("utf-8")).digest())
    d[6] = (d[6] & 0x0F) | 0x30
    d[8] = (d[8] & 0x3F) | 0x80
    return str(uuid.UUID(bytes=bytes(d)))


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ plan
@dataclass
class LaunchPlan:
    java: Path
    args: list[str]                       # everything after java (JVM args, -cp, main class, game args)
    cwd: Path
    classpath: list[Path] = field(default_factory=list)
    natives_dir: Path | None = None
    job_file: Path | None = None
    mod_jar: Path | None = None
    mod_mode: str = "addMods"             # addMods | installed
    missing: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    notes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)

    @property
    def command(self) -> list[str]:
        return [str(self.java), *self.args]

    def as_text(self) -> str:
        return subprocess.list2cmdline(self.command)


def build_plan(job_file: str | Path, token: str | None = None, *, mc_dir: Path = MC_DIR, version: str = VERSION_NAME,
               username: str = DEFAULT_USERNAME, game_uuid: str | None = None, xmx: str = DEFAULT_XMX, xms: str = DEFAULT_XMS,
               mod_jar: str | Path | None = None, extra_jvm: list[str] | None = None, width: int | None = None,
               height: int | None = None) -> LaunchPlan:
    job_file = Path(job_file).resolve()
    vdir = mc_dir / "versions" / version
    v = load_version(mc_dir, version)
    missing: list[str] = []
    notes: list[str] = []

    def need(p: Path, what: str) -> Path:
        if not p.exists():
            missing.append(f"{what}: {p}")
        return p

    java = need(mc_dir / "runtime" / "java-runtime-delta" / "windows" / "java-runtime-delta" / "bin" / "java.exe", "java")
    need(job_file, "job file")

    # classpath: libraries (v.libraries order) + client jar
    libs_dir = mc_dir / "libraries"
    cp: list[Path] = []
    seen: set[str] = set()
    for lib in v["libraries"]:
        p = library_path(lib, libs_dir)
        if p is None or str(p).lower() in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(str(p).lower())
        need(p, "library")
        cp.append(p)
    add = vdir / "TLauncherAdditional.json"
    jar_name = (_read_json(add).get("jar") if add.is_file() else None) or v.get("jar") or version
    client_jar = need(mc_dir / "versions" / jar_name / f"{jar_name}.jar", "client jar")
    cp.append(client_jar)

    # natives
    natives = vdir / "natives"
    if not natives.is_dir() or not any(natives.glob("lwjgl*.dll")):
        natives = HERE / "natives"
        notes.append(f"TLauncher natives dir missing, LWJGL will self-extract into {natives}")
        natives.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) if False else None  # dry run never creates folders; launch() does

    assets = mc_dir / "assets"
    index_id = v.get("assetIndex", {}).get("id") or v.get("assets")
    need(assets / "indexes" / f"{index_id}.json", "asset index")
    log_cfg = None
    lg = (v.get("logging") or {}).get("client")
    if lg and lg.get("file", {}).get("id"):
        log_cfg = assets / "log_configs" / lg["file"]["id"]
        if not log_cfg.exists():
            notes.append(f"log4j config {log_cfg.name} missing, using default logging")
            log_cfg = None

    # mod jar injection
    jar = Path(mod_jar).resolve() if mod_jar else DEFAULT_MOD_JAR
    installed = [p for p in (mc_dir / "mods").glob("flashback_auto*.jar")] if (mc_dir / "mods").is_dir() else []
    mod_mode = "installed" if installed else "addMods"
    if mod_mode == "addMods":
        need(jar, "mod jar (build it: python tools/flashback_auto/build.py)")
    else:
        notes.append(f"mod jar already installed in mods/: {installed[0].name}; -Dfabric.addMods not used")

    subst = {
        "auth_player_name": username,
        "version_name": version,
        "game_directory": str(mc_dir),
        "assets_root": str(assets),
        "assets_index_name": str(index_id),
        "auth_uuid": game_uuid or offline_uuid(username),
        "auth_access_token": "0",
        "clientid": "0",
        "auth_xuid": "0",
        "version_type": str(v.get("type", "release")),
        "natives_directory": str(natives),
        "launcher_name": "flashback_auto",
        "launcher_version": MOD_VERSION,
        "classpath": os.pathsep.join(str(p) for p in cp),
        "user_type": "legacy",
        "resolution_width": str(width or ""),
        "resolution_height": str(height or ""),
    }

    def sub(s: str) -> str:
        return re.sub(r"\$\{(\w+)\}", lambda m: subst.get(m.group(1), m.group(0)), s)

    features = {"has_custom_resolution": bool(width and height)}
    jvm = [sub(a) for a in _args(v.get("arguments", {}).get("jvm", []), features)]
    game = [sub(a) for a in _args(v.get("arguments", {}).get("game", []), features)]
    left = [a for a in jvm + game if re.search(r"\$\{\w+\}", a)]
    if left:
        missing.append(f"unresolved placeholders: {left}")
    if "--userType" not in game:
        game += ["--userType", "legacy"]

    ours = [f"-Xmx{xmx}", f"-Xms{xms}", "-XX:+UseG1GC", "-Dfile.encoding=UTF-8",
            f"-D{'flashback_auto.job'}={job_file}"]
    if token:
        ours.append(f"-Dflashback_auto.token={token}")
    if mod_mode == "addMods":
        ours.append(f"-Dfabric.addMods={jar}")
    if log_cfg:
        ours.append(f"-Dlog4j.configurationFile={log_cfg}")
    ours += list(extra_jvm or [])

    # JVM args from the profile go first, ours after (later -X flags win), then -cp is already inside `jvm`
    args = ours + jvm + [v["mainClass"]] + game
    return LaunchPlan(java=java, args=args, cwd=mc_dir, classpath=cp, natives_dir=natives, job_file=job_file,
                      mod_jar=jar if mod_mode == "addMods" else installed[0], mod_mode=mod_mode, missing=missing, notes=notes)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ safety checks
def _powershell_processes() -> list[dict]:
    script = ("@(Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter \"Name='javaw.exe' OR Name='java.exe'\" | ForEach-Object "
              "{ [pscustomobject]@{pid=[int]$_.ProcessId;name=$_.Name;cmd=[string]$_.CommandLine} }) | ConvertTo-Json -Compress")
    try:
        r = subprocess.run(["powershell", "-NoProfile", "-NonInteractive", "-Command", script], capture_output=True, text=True,
                           timeout=30, creationflags=CREATE_NO_WINDOW, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired) as e:
        raise LaunchError(f"cannot list running processes ({e}); refusing to launch blind") from e
    out = (r.stdout or "").strip()
    if not out:
        return []
    try:
        d = json.loads(out)
    except ValueError as e:
        raise LaunchError(f"cannot parse the process list ({out[:100]!r}); refusing to launch blind") from e
    return [d] if isinstance(d, dict) else list(d)


def running_minecraft(list_processes=None) -> list[dict]:
    """java/javaw processes whose command line mentions minecraft (the TLauncher game or ours)."""
    procs = (list_processes or _powershell_processes)()
    hits = []
    for p in procs:
        cmd = (p.get("cmd") or "").lower()
        if "minecraft" in cmd:
            hits.append({"pid": p.get("pid"), "name": p.get("name"), "cmd": (p.get("cmd") or "")[:200]})
    return hits


def check_plan(plan: LaunchPlan) -> list[str]:
    """Problems that would stop a launch (missing files)."""
    return list(plan.missing)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ arming
def write_armed(job_file: str | Path, token: str | None = None, now: float | None = None) -> Path:
    """Write ``ARMED`` next to the job file. The mod needs this AND -Dflashback_auto.job (and matching token) to do anything."""
    job_file = Path(job_file).resolve()
    p = job_file.with_name(ARMED)
    body = {"job": str(job_file), "created": int(now if now is not None else time.time()), "pid": os.getpid()}
    if token:
        body["token"] = token
    p.write_text(json.dumps(body), encoding="utf-8")
    return p


def disarm(job_file: str | Path) -> None:
    try:
        Path(job_file).resolve().with_name(ARMED).unlink()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        pass


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ launching
class GameProcess:
    """Thin wrapper over the Popen handle (also what tests replace with a fake)."""

    def __init__(self, popen: subprocess.Popen):
        self._p = popen
        self.pid = popen.pid

    def poll(self):
        return self._p.poll()

    def wait(self, timeout=None):
        return self._p.wait(timeout)

    def kill_tree(self) -> None:
        if self._p.poll() is None:
            subprocess.run(["taskkill", "/PID", str(self.pid), "/T", "/F"], capture_output=True, creationflags=CREATE_NO_WINDOW)
            try:
                self._p.wait(15)
            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                self._p.kill()


def launch(plan: LaunchPlan, log_path: str | Path | None = None, *, list_processes=None, popen=subprocess.Popen) -> GameProcess:
    """Start the game. Refuses on missing files or when another Minecraft is running."""
    probs = check_plan(plan)
    if probs:
        raise LaunchError("cannot launch, missing:\n  " + "\n  ".join(probs))
    other = running_minecraft(list_processes)
    if other:
        raise LaunchError("another Minecraft is already running, not launching: "
                          + "; ".join(f"pid {o['pid']} {o['name']}" for o in other))
    if plan.natives_dir and not plan.natives_dir.exists():
        plan.natives_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out = open(log_path, "ab") if log_path else subprocess.DEVNULL
    try:
        p = popen(plan.command, cwd=str(plan.cwd), stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=out, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
                  creationflags=CREATE_NO_WINDOW | BELOW_NORMAL_PRIORITY_CLASS | CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP)
    finally:
        if log_path:
            out.close()
    return GameProcess(p)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ cli
def _redact(cmd: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    out = []
    skip = False
    for a in cmd:
        if skip:
            out.append("***")
            skip = False
            continue
        out.append(a)
        if a == "--accessToken":
            skip = True
    return out


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("--job", required=True, help="job file written by flashback_keyframes.jobs_json")
    ap.add_argument("--launch", action="store_true", help="really start Minecraft (default: dry run)")
    ap.add_argument("--arm", action="store_true", help="with --launch: write the ARMED marker first (the exporter normally does this)")
    ap.add_argument("--xmx", default=DEFAULT_XMX)
    ap.add_argument("--username", default=DEFAULT_USERNAME)
    ap.add_argument("--mod-jar", default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="print the plan as JSON")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)

    token = uuid.uuid4().hex if a.launch else "DRYRUN"
    plan = build_plan(a.job, token, username=a.username, xmx=a.xmx, mod_jar=a.mod_jar)
    if a.json:
        print(json.dumps({"java": str(plan.java), "args": _redact(plan.args), "cwd": str(plan.cwd), "missing": plan.missing,
                          "notes": plan.notes, "mod_mode": plan.mod_mode}, indent=2))
    else:
        print("mode:", "LAUNCH" if a.launch else "dry run (nothing started)")
        print("java:", plan.java)
        print("cwd :", plan.cwd)
        print("mod :", plan.mod_jar, f"({plan.mod_mode})")
        print("classpath entries:", len(plan.classpath), "| natives:", plan.natives_dir)
        for n in plan.notes:
            print("note:", n)
        print("command:")
        print(subprocess.list2cmdline(_redact(plan.command)))
    if plan.missing:
        print(f"\nPROBLEMS ({len(plan.missing)}):", file=sys.stderr)
        for m in plan.missing:
            print("  -", m, file=sys.stderr)
    else:
        print(f"\nOK: all {len(plan.classpath)} classpath files, java, assets index and mod jar exist.")
    if not a.launch:
        return 1 if plan.missing else 0
    if a.arm:
        write_armed(a.job, token)
    try:
        proc = launch(plan, Path(a.job).resolve().with_name("game_stdout.log"))
    except LaunchError as e:
        print("REFUSED:", e, file=sys.stderr)
        if a.arm:
            disarm(a.job)
        return 2
    print(f"started pid {proc.pid}; status: {Path(a.job).resolve().with_name('status.json')}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

class FakeProc:
    """Stands in for the Minecraft process. `script(job_path, proc)` runs in a thread and plays the mod's role."""
    def __init__(self, job_path, script=None, exit_after_script=True):
        self.pid = 4242
        self.job = Path(job_path)
        self.killed = False
        self.rc = None
        self._done = threading.Event()
        self.exit_after_script = exit_after_script
        self.t = threading.Thread(target=self._run, args=(script,), daemon=True)
        if script:
            self.t.start()

    def _run(self, script):
        try:
            script(self.job, self)
        finally:
            if self.exit_after_script and self.rc is None and not self.killed:
                self.rc = 0

    def poll(self):
        return self.rc

    def kill_tree(self):
        self.killed = True
        self.rc = 1

    st = {"modVersion": "0.1.0", "state": "starting", "message": "", "pid": 1, "updatedMs": int(time.time() * 1000),
          "jobIndex": -1, "jobCount": 0, "job": None, "progressPct": 0, "frames": 0, "totalFrames": 0, "results": [], "errors": []}
    st.update(kw)
    tmpf = job.with_name("status.json.tmp")
    tmpf.write_text(json.dumps(st), encoding="utf-8")
    tmpf.replace(job.with_name("status.json"))

        time.sleep(0.15)
        out = Path(s["output"])
        out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

                        "frames": 120, "durationS": 2.0, "wallS": 5.0, "message": ""})

"""flashback_auto driver tests (no Minecraft is started). Run from studio/:  .venv/Scripts/python.exe tests/test_flashback_export.py"""
import json
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import threading
import time
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))
from mcstudio import flashback_export as FE  # noqa: E402

L = FE.launcher()
tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="fa_test_"))
passed: list[str] = []


def ok(msg: str):
    passed.append(msg)
    print("  ok -", msg)


def make_replay(name="replay.zip") -> Path:
    p = tmp / name
    with zipfile.ZipFile(p, "w") as z:
        z.writestr("metadata.json", json.dumps({"uuid": "11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555", "total_ticks": 3000}))
    return p


def make_job(folder: Path, n=2, replay: Path | None = None, **over) -> Path:
    folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    replay = replay or make_replay()
    jobs = []
    for i in range(n):
        j = {"scene": i, "name": f"{i:02d}_orbit", "start": 100 + i * 200, "end": 220 + i * 200,
             "output": str(folder / "out" / f"{i:02d}_orbit.mp4"), "width": 1920, "height": 1080, "fps": 60.0,
             "container": "MP4", "codec": "H264", "encoder": None, "bitrate": 20000000, "ssaa": False, "noGui": True,
             "resetRng": False, "recordAudio": False, "transparent": False, "kind": "orbit", "note": ""}
        j.update(over)
        jobs.append(j)
    p = folder / "jobs.json"
    p.write_text(json.dumps({"version": 1, "replay": str(replay), "jobs": jobs}), encoding="utf-8")
    return p


def expect_job_error(data, what):
    p = tmp / "bad_jobs.json"
    p.write_text(json.dumps(data) if not isinstance(data, str) else data, encoding="utf-8")
    try:
        FE.parse_jobs(p)
    except FE.JobFileError:
        return
    raise AssertionError(f"should reject: {what}")


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ fakes
class FakeProc:
    """Stands in for the Minecraft process. `script(job_path, proc)` runs in a thread and plays the mod's role."""
    def __init__(self, job_path, script=None, exit_after_script=True):
        self.pid = 4242
        self.job = Path(job_path)
        self.killed = False
        self.rc = None
        self._done = threading.Event()
        self.exit_after_script = exit_after_script
        self.t = threading.Thread(target=self._run, args=(script,), daemon=True)
        if script:
            self.t.start()

    def _run(self, script):
        try:
            script(self.job, self)
        finally:
            if self.exit_after_script and self.rc is None and not self.killed:
                self.rc = 0

    def poll(self):
        return self.rc

    def kill_tree(self):
        self.killed = True
        self.rc = 1


def write_status(job: Path, **kw):
    st = {"modVersion": "0.1.0", "state": "starting", "message": "", "pid": 1, "updatedMs": int(time.time() * 1000),
          "jobIndex": -1, "jobCount": 0, "job": None, "progressPct": 0, "frames": 0, "totalFrames": 0, "results": [], "errors": []}
    st.update(kw)
    tmpf = job.with_name("status.json.tmp")
    tmpf.write_text(json.dumps(st), encoding="utf-8")
    tmpf.replace(job.with_name("status.json"))


def good_script(job: Path, proc: FakeProc):
    jf = FE.parse_jobs(job)
    results = []
    write_status(job, state="starting", jobCount=len(jf.shots))
    time.sleep(0.15)
    write_status(job, state="opening", jobCount=len(jf.shots))
    time.sleep(0.15)
    for i, s in enumerate(jf.shots):
        write_status(job, state="exporting", jobIndex=i, jobCount=len(jf.shots), job=s["name"], progressPct=50, results=results)
        time.sleep(0.15)
        out = Path(s["output"])
        out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        out.write_bytes(b"x" * 1000)
        results.append({"index": i, "name": s["name"], "scene": s["scene"], "output": str(out), "ok": True, "bytes": 1000,
                        "frames": 120, "durationS": 2.0, "wallS": 5.0, "message": ""})
    write_status(job, state="done", jobIndex=len(jf.shots) - 1, jobCount=len(jf.shots), progressPct=100, results=results)


def exporter(**kw) -> FE.FlashbackAutoExporter:
    jar = tmp / "flashback_auto-0.1.0.jar"
    jar.write_bytes(b"PK")
    d = dict(launch=True, mod_jar=jar, poll_s=0.05, startup_timeout_s=1.5, stale_status_s=1.5, exit_grace_s=1.0,
             stop_grace_s=0.6, list_processes=lambda: [])
    d.update(kw)
    return FE.FlashbackAutoExporter(**d)

def test_job_parsing():
    job = make_job(tmp / "p1", n=2)
    jf = FE.parse_jobs(job)
    assert len(jf.shots) == 2 and jf.watchdog_s == 2700 and jf.replay.name == "replay.zip"
    good = json.loads(job.read_text())
    for what, mut in [
        ("version", lambda d: d.update(version=2)),
        ("container", lambda d: d["jobs"][0].update(container="EXE")),
        ("codec", lambda d: d["jobs"][0].update(codec="H999")),
        ("range", lambda d: d["jobs"][0].update(start=300, end=100)),
        ("odd width", lambda d: d["jobs"][0].update(width=1921)),
        ("fps", lambda d: d["jobs"][0].update(fps=1000)),
        ("extension", lambda d: d["jobs"][0].update(output=d["jobs"][0]["output"].replace(".mp4", ".avi"))),
        ("name", lambda d: d["jobs"][0].update(name="../evil")),
        ("relative output", lambda d: d["jobs"][0].update(output="rel.mp4")),
        ("missing replay", lambda d: d.update(replay=str(tmp / "nope.zip"))),
        ("no jobs", lambda d: d.update(jobs=[])),
        ("duplicate output", lambda d: d["jobs"][1].update(output=d["jobs"][0]["output"])),
        ("start without end", lambda d: d["jobs"][0].update(end=None)),
    ]:
        d = json.loads(json.dumps(good))
        mut(d)
        expect_job_error(d, what)
    expect_job_error("{{{", "garbage")
    expect_job_error("[1]", "not an object")
    # tick range may be left to the scene
    d = json.loads(json.dumps(good))
    d["jobs"][0].update(start=None, end=None)
    p = tmp / "scene_range.json"
    p.write_text(json.dumps(d))
    assert FE.parse_jobs(p).shots[0]["start"] is None
    # what flashback_keyframes.jobs_json produces is accepted
    from mcstudio import flashback_keyframes as FK
    jj = FK.jobs_json(make_replay("fk.zip"), [FK.Shot(name="orbit", kind="orbit", start=100, end=220, tracks=[])], tmp / "fk_out")
    p = tmp / "fk_jobs.json"

    assert FE.parse_jobs(p).shots[0]["name"] == "00_orbit"

def test_armed_logic():
    job = make_job(tmp / "armed")
    marker = job.with_name("ARMED")
    now = time.time()
    assert FE.armed_check(None) == (False, "no -Dflashback_auto.job")
    assert not FE.armed_check(str(job))[0]                                  # no marker
    L.write_armed(job, "tok", now)
    assert FE.armed_check(str(job), "tok")[0]
    assert not FE.armed_check(str(job), "other")[0]                         # token mismatch
    assert not FE.armed_check(str(job), None)[0]                            # token not passed to JVM
    L.write_armed(job, None, now - 601)
    assert not FE.armed_check(str(job))[0]                                  # stale
    L.write_armed(job, None, now - 599)
    assert FE.armed_check(str(job))[0]
    L.write_armed(job, None, now + 3600)
    assert not FE.armed_check(str(job))[0]                                  # future
    marker.write_text(json.dumps({"job": str(tmp / "other.json"), "created": int(now)}))
    assert not FE.armed_check(str(job))[0]                                  # names another job
    marker.write_text("garbage")
    assert not FE.armed_check(str(job))[0]
    L.disarm(job)
    assert not marker.exists()
    L.disarm(job)                                                           # idempotent
    ok("ARMED logic: missing / stale / future / mismatched job / bad token / garbage -> inert; fresh -> armed")


def test_armed_matches_java():
    """The marker the Python side writes is judged identically by the compiled Java class (skipped if the mod is not built)."""
    classes = FE.STUDIO / "tools" / "flashback_auto" / "build" / "classes"
    tclasses = FE.STUDIO / "tools" / "flashback_auto" / "build" / "test-classes"
    java = FE.MC_DIR / "runtime/java-runtime-delta/windows/java-runtime-delta/bin/java.exe"
    gson = FE.MC_DIR / "libraries/com/google/code/gson/gson/2.13.2/gson-2.13.2.jar"
    if not (classes.exists() and tclasses.exists() and java.exists() and gson.exists()):
        print("  skip - mod not built (python tools/flashback_auto/build.py)")
        return
    job = make_job(tmp / "javaarm")
    cp = ";".join(map(str, [classes, tclasses, gson]))

    def java_says(token=None):
        cmd = [str(java), "-cp", cp, "dev.crodie.flashbackauto.SelfTest", "armed", str(job)] + ([token] if token else [])
        r = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
        return r.returncode == 0, r.stdout.strip()
    assert java_says()[0] is False                                          # no marker
    L.write_armed(job, "t1")
    assert java_says("t1")[0] is True and java_says("zz")[0] is False and java_says()[0] is False
    L.write_armed(job, "t1", time.time() - 700)
    assert java_says("t1")[0] is False
    L.disarm(job)
    ok("ARMED: Python-written marker is accepted/rejected identically by the Java ArmedCheck")


def test_status_monitoring_and_results():
    job = make_job(tmp / "good", n=2)
    spawned = []

    def spawn(plan, log):
        assert job.with_name("ARMED").exists(), "ARMED must exist before the game starts"
        ok_, why = FE.armed_check(str(job), _token_of(plan))
        assert ok_, why                                                      # the mod would accept this launch
        p = FakeProc(job, good_script)
        spawned.append(p)
        return p
    res = exporter(spawn=spawn).export(job, out_dir=job.parent / "out", timeout_s=30)

    assert not job.with_name("ARMED").exists(), "ARMED must be removed afterwards"
    assert not spawned[0].killed
    ok("status monitoring: done -> 2 ok results, ARMED present while running and removed after")


def _token_of(plan) -> str:

        if a.startswith("-Dflashback_auto.token="):
            return a.split("=", 1)[1]
    raise AssertionError("no token arg")

def test_overall_timeout_kills():
    job = make_job(tmp / "slow", n=1)

    def script(j, proc):                         # keeps reporting progress forever
        while not proc.killed:
            write_status(j, state="exporting", progressPct=10)
            time.sleep(0.05)
    procs = []

    def spawn(plan, log):
        p = FakeProc(job, script, exit_after_script=False)
        procs.append(p)
        return p
    res = exporter(spawn=spawn).export(job, timeout_s=0.8)
    assert procs[0].killed and "timeout" in res[0].message, res[0].message
    ok("overall timeout while exporting -> killed")

def test_stop_file_and_request_stop():

        time.sleep(0.2)

        while not proc.killed:

def test_refuses_when_minecraft_running():

def test_dry_run_command_valid():
    if not FE.MC_DIR.exists():
        print("  skip - no .minecraft on this machine")
        return
    job = make_job(tmp / "plan", n=1)
    jar = tmp / "flashback_auto-0.1.0.jar"
    jar.write_bytes(b"PK")
    plan = L.build_plan(job, "tok123", mod_jar=jar)
    assert not plan.missing, plan.missing
    cmd = plan.command
    assert Path(cmd[0]).name == "java.exe" and Path(cmd[0]).exists()
    assert "net.fabricmc.loader.impl.launch.knot.KnotClient" in cmd
    assert f"-Dflashback_auto.job={job.resolve()}" in cmd and "-Dflashback_auto.token=tok123" in cmd
    assert any(a.startswith("-Dfabric.addMods=") and str(jar.resolve()) in a for a in cmd) or plan.mod_mode == "installed"
    assert "-Xmx6G" in cmd and "--accessToken" in cmd and cmd[cmd.index("--accessToken") + 1] == "0"
    assert cmd[cmd.index("--username") + 1] == "papiguapo" and cmd[cmd.index("--version") + 1] == "Fabric 1.21.11"
    assert cmd[cmd.index("--gameDir") + 1] == str(FE.MC_DIR) and cmd[cmd.index("--assetIndex") + 1]
    assert "--userType" in cmd and "${" not in " ".join(cmd)
    cp = cmd[cmd.index("-cp") + 1].split(";")
    assert all(Path(c).exists() for c in cp) and len(cp) > 40
    assert not any("natives-linux" in c or "natives-macos" in c or "arm64" in c or "natives-windows-x86" in c for c in cp)
    assert any(c.endswith("1.21.11.jar") for c in cp) and any("fabric-loader" in c for c in cp)
    # offline uuid is the Java nameUUIDFromBytes convention (version 3)
    assert L.offline_uuid("papiguapo")[14] == "3"
    ok(f"dry-run command valid: {len(cp)} classpath files exist, KnotClient, job/token/addMods props, offline auth")

    plan = L.LaunchPlan(java=Path(sys.executable), args=["-version"], cwd=tmp)
